items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. After protesting for 16 days, around 500 sanitation workers temporarily called off their agitation on September 4, following talks with several ministers and Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) officials. Several of their immediate demands, including food allowances, toilets and resting facilities for women workers, safety equipment and withdrawal of cases, have been assured. However, their central demand — permanent employment — remains unresolved. The protest began on August 20 near the Allikulam court complex gate at the GCC headquarters in Ripon Building. What has been promised? According to Bharathi, the state government has agreed to provide a Rs 50 food allowance per day from October 1. items.summary: The Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal (KSAT) at Kalburgi has stayed the suspension of a government school teacher who participated in a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) event [Gururaj v. State of Karnataka]. A coram of Judicial Member SY Watawati and Administrative Member Dr Amita Prasad said that the school teacher had not violated the Karnataka State Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 2021 that prevents government servants from attending functions organised by political parties or by associations that participate in politics. The Tribunal further held the applicant had not violated any State government order or notification that explicitly barred participation in events. It further held the RSS to be a non-political party. "When he participated in the event organized by a non-political party, the act of the applicant did not violate the conditions stipulated under Rule 5 of the Conduct Rules, 2021 referred to supra. Further, the State Government has not issued any order or notification prohibiting any Government Official from participating in such an event." items.title: BJP’s violent meme war: The attacks on opponents and dissenters as ‘Dimagi Naxals’
items.summary: Following a restructuring of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) digital wing, the party has intensified its social media campaigning, increasingly employing violent memes and videos. On August 27, the Karnataka unit of the BJP shared a meme featuring a clip from the film ‘KGF: Chapter 2’, in which the protagonist unleashes a barrage of gunfire on his opponents. In the meme, the shooters were depicted as the BJP’s state units, while the opponents were labeled ‘Dimagi Naxals’ — a term used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his Independence Day speech to describe individuals with a “Naxalite mindset”. The accompanying caption stated, “We will not stop, we are confronting ‘Urban Naxals’ with full force.” The BJP Karnataka unit posted this video on Instagram as a collaborative post with the BJP units of Delhi, Goa, and Jammu & Kashmir. No slowing down - taking on "Dimaagi Naxals" with full force! https://t.co/cYhIZmKJ6E pic.twitter.com/iqANzyrBRT — BJP Karnataka (@BJP4Karnataka) August 27, 2026 The Chhattisgarh BJP posted a clip from the web series ‘Mirzapur’ in which the character ‘Munna Bhaiya’ repeatedly slaps a student. In the clip, the student is portrayed as a ‘Dimagi Naxal’.

items.title: Falsely implicated in Sarla Bhat's murder but give me capital punishment: Yasin Malik to Kashmir court
items.summary: Jailed Kashmiri separatist and Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front (JKLF) chief Yasin Malik has filed an affidavit before a Jammu and Kashmir court denying any role in the 1990 murder of Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat. Malik has said that he has decided not to contest the trial proceedings. Instead, he has requested capital punishment for himself while maintaining that he is innocent and has been “falsely implicated” in the case more than three decades after the murder. “The prosecution's present narrative resembles a fictional story rather than a genuine criminal investigation, carefully woven together after several decades solely with the object of falsely implicating me in the present case. It finds no support from the contemporaneous record or the conduct of the investigating agencies during the relevant period,” Yasin said in his affidavit. He added that he got to know of Bhat’s murder months after the incident. “I respectfully state that I first came to know of the murder of Ms. Sarla Bhat on 21 February 1991, while I was in judicial custody. items.summary: Courts must decide cases based on the evidence before them rather than public opinion or narratives circulating on social media or newspapers, former Supreme Court Justice Rajesh Bindal recently said. Justice Bindal stressed the need for a gender-neutral criminal justice system and also said that courts must focus on the material before them rather than public perceptions or allegations of bias. “We have to do justice by seeing what is there on that court before us. It is not that what is said in the social media or what is said in the newspaper or what is said outside the board by anyone. items.title: Bengaluru’s parks are under threat | Let Me Explain 159 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: What can you do in 20 mins? If you are in Bengaluru, it could take longer to cover just one kilometre in a car. Could take longer to get a cup of filter coffee But that’s all the time it took the Karnataka legislature to introduce a law that could dismantle environmental protections to parks. No floor debate. No public conversation. Just a fast-tracked amendment that gives executive committees a permanent key to carve up 5% of any state park. So technically, a metro station or a concrete building for–say– the district administration or even a parking lot can be built here. "5%" sounds like a small, harmless number. But let's do the math. Lalbagh spans roughly 240 acres. Five percent of that is 12 full acres. I am not saying this hasn't been done before. Earlier governments have passed specific, project-by-project exceptions to take park land But those were individual bypasses, debated on their own merits. What this new law does is create a blanket, permanent key For now, after much outrage, CM DK Shivakumar has taken a step back. Promising to 'reconsider' the amendment in the upcoming session. items.title: [Courting Controversy] Down the rabbit hole: Policing Wonderland for kids
items.summary: Lewis Carroll gave us the phrase "down the rabbit hole" in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, long before anyone had even heard of the term algorithm. And yet, today, it is hard to think of a better description for what a YouTube autoplay queue or an Instagram Reels feed can do to a 10-year-old’s fantasy on a lazy Sunday afternoon. Alice, at least, could climb her way out of the rabbit hole. Today’s metaphorical wonderland, that is online social media platforms, are specifically engineered to keep users engaged for hours making sure that no one finds a way out. It is this engineered descent that lies behind the familiar observation that the technology which connects us also controls us. A recent writ petition filed before the Delhi High Court concerning the impact of social media usage on children brought this to the fore. The writ filed against the Union of India sought sweeping relief in the form of age-appropriate restrictions on social media access for children, viable age-verification mechanisms modelled on the Digi Yatra system, curfews on teenage platform use, and stricter enforcement of existing legislation, including the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Digital Pers

items.title: Calcutta High Court orders family pension to be split equally between two wives of deceased employee
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court recently held that where a deceased Central government employee leaves behind two wives, both are entitled to receive family pension in equal shares under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules [ Rina Yasmin vs The Union of India & Ors. ]. Justice Reetobroto Kumar Mitra observed that the statutory rules explicitly provide for an equal division of pension between the surviving wives, while gratuity must be paid only to the validly designated nominee. "As far as the payment of family pension is concerned, the same is covered under said Rule 50(8)(c)... This rule stipulates that in the event the employee has more than one wife, in the case of two wives, the family pension shall be paid to both wives in equal shares," the Court observed in its September 2 order. The ruling came on a plea moved by the first wife (petitioner) of a Central Ground Water Board employee who died in service in 2024. The employee had two wives and was governed by Muslim personal law. The first wife had approached authorities seeking family pension, death gratuity, and compassionate appointment. items.summary: Court-annexed arbitration centres should eventually become independent of the courts that establish them, Senior Advocate Shashank Garg said while discussing the future of institutional arbitration in India. Garg said court supervision gives a newly established arbitration centre immediate credibility. However, he added that the long-term goal should be to reduce judicial control and allow such institutions to function independently. He was speaking at a session on institutional arbitration during GHAC Arbitration Week 2026, organised by the High Court of Gujarat in collaboration with the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre. The session was moderated by Senior Advocate Ritin Rai . The panel also included Vivekananda Neelakantan , Registrar, Singapore International Arbitration Centre; Khushboo Deshmukh , Deputy Director, South Asia, ICC International Court of Arbitration; and Vyapak Desai , Advocate and Member, Mumbai Centre for International Arbitration. items.title: ‘Aasmani’ plagiarism row: Mumbai court restrains publication of defamatory content against Sayani Gupta
items.summary: A Mumbai city civil court on Thursday barred the publication of defamatory material against actor and filmmaker Sayani Gupta over her short film Aasmani [ Sayani Gupta v Vinita Negi & Ors. ]. Additional Sessions Judge Shudhirkumar Murlidharrao Bukke allowed an application filed by Gupta for such interim relied. The interim order was passed on a ₹9 crore defamation suit filed by Gupta against filmmaker Vinita Negi after the latter claimed that key elements of Gupta's film were plagiarised. The court yesterday allowed Gupta's plea to restrain Negi and other defendants from publishing, circulating or continuing to publish defamatory material against her. The interim relief granted would also include the removal of defamatory content from the platforms of defendants such as Meta, Reddit and the Deccan Chronicle. The court, however, clarified that its interim order would not mean a blanket ban on publishing information that is based on true facts. “The defendant no. 1(Negi) has every right to take legal action against the plaintiff (Gupta) and she is at liberty to publish any contents based on true facts. items.title: Office we hold is temporary, institutions must endure: Chhattisgarh HC Chief Justice Ramesh Sinha retires
items.summary: Chief Justice Ramesh Sinha of the Chhattisgarh High Court on Thursday demitted office, marking the end of a judicial career spanning nearly 15 years. A farewell reference was organised by the Chhattisgarh High Court to mark his retirement. Speaking at the event, Chief Justice Sinha reflected on his tenure, the responsibilities attached to the judicial office and spoke at length about building a strong judicial institution for those who serve it and for those who will carry it forward. " The office we hold is temporary, the people who occupy them come and go, but institutions must endure and therefore our ultimate responsibility is not to leave behind a personal legacy but to leave behind a stronger institution, great trust and a better future for those who will come after us, " he said. Chief Justice Ramesh Sinha Our ultimate responsibility is not to leave behind a personal legacy but to leave behind a stronger institution. Chief Justice Sinha was born on September 5, 1964. He enrolled as an advocate in September 1990 and practiced before the Allahabad High Court. He was elevated as an additional judge of the High Court in November 2011 and became a permanent judge in August 2013.
